notes: Iteration 3 uses stricter assertions based on real SA call feedback: diagnose before prescribing, don't invent numbers, treat cache as healthy
Eval 0 (memory leak): with-skill 100% vs baseline 67%. Baseline missed collection count check and version upgrade.

Eval 1 (high memory): with-skill 40% vs baseline 0%. Both still provide estimates before asking config, but with-skill at least mentions full-text indexes and metrics. Baseline invents extensive GB figures.
Eval 2 (quantization): with-skill 83% vs baseline 17%. Baseline recommends always_ram=False and doesn't mention full-text indexes. With-skill correctly warns against it.
The 'don't invent numbers' assertion is the hardest for both versions. Models want to provide estimates even when the skill says not to.
Compared to iteration 2: assertions are much more discriminating. Baseline dropped from 83% to 29%, showing the old assertions were too easy.
